draft.title: Review Halcyon Staffing invoice against contract and approved timecards

rules.text: No employee may appear on more than one labor line for the same week ending date.

citations.quote: And nobody should be billed twice for the same week.

rules.text: For each labor line, billed hours must be less than or equal to the approved_hours shown on that employee's timecard for the billed week.

citations.quote: Then I check each person's hours against their timecard.
Billed hours can't go over that.

rules.text: If any check fails, recommend disputing the invoice and requesting a credit; otherwise the invoice passes review.

citations.quote: If anything is off, I dispute it and ask for a credit.

rules.text: Sign in to the Halcyon Staffing client portal, open the invoices list, and open the invoice under review by its invoice number.

For each person billed on the invoice, click that line's "View timecard" link to open the employee's timecard for the billed week, read the approved_hours field, then return to the invoice before opening the next person's timecard.

citations.quote: Then I check each person's hours against their timecard.

open_questions: Where are the contract rates found? The reviewer says every rate must match the contract but never opens it, and no per-role rates were stated.
How should duplicate billing for the same week be detected? It was stated as a rule but not demonstrated.
How is a dispute filed and a credit requested? This was not demonstrated.
Does a small difference (e.g. rounding) count as "off", or is any difference a failure?
Which non-labor charges are allowed and what are their caps? None were stated in the recording.
Where on the invoice page are each line's billed hours and bill rate read? The portal_map has no selectors for these, and no click on them was recorded.
Are the spoken approvals (Maya 40, Sam 36) meant as fixed per-person limits, or only as readings of that week's timecard? How do Maya and Sam map to employee IDs E-101 and E-104?
Does the week parameter (e.g. 2026-10-11) mean the week-ending date or the week-start date when matching invoice lines for the duplicate check?
Is any additional information on the timecard page (e.g. actual worked hours) to be compared, or only the approved_hours field?

rule.text: Every labor line's hourly bill rate must equal the contract rate card rate for that line's role.

citations.quote: Every rate on it has to match our contract.

dropped.reason: invented: u2 only says every rate must match the contract. Keying the comparison to a 'rate card' and to 'that line's role' adds structure the recording never mentions; no roles or rate card were said or shown.

verdicts.reason: u2 only says every rate must match the contract. Keying the comparison to a 'rate card' and to 'that line's role' adds structure the recording never mentions; no roles or rate card were said or shown.
u3 says nobody should be billed twice for the same week. One small detail is interpretation: calling the week a 'week ending date' is an assumption, since the URL only shows week=2026-10-11.
u4 says hours are checked against the timecard and u6 says billed hours can't go over the approved amount. Steps 14 and 16 show opening the timecard and reading the approved_hours field.
u8 says that if anything is off, the reviewer disputes it and asks for a credit. The 'otherwise passes' branch is the implied complement.
Steps 0–11 show the login form, submitting it, navigating to /portal/invoices and clicking invoice HSG-1010.
Steps 14–23 show clicking 'View timecard', reading approved_hours (40, 36), and returning to the invoice between employees. u4 backs doing this for each person.
